title: Taming Deadly Feedback in Reinforcement Learning

beats.text: What happens when your vector database only sees isolated chunks? Taming Deadly Feedback in Reinforcement Learning fixes retrieval with a 140% boost.
beats.visual_focus: Chalkboard showing raw Atari pixel frames pouring into a neural net, causing weights to violently explode with red error warnings.

visual_blueprint.title: DEADLY FEEDBACK INSTABILITY
visual_blueprint.sub: Raw frame inputs causing immediate gradient divergence

motif_params.title: DEADLY FEEDBACK INSTABILITY
motif_params.sub: Raw frame inputs causing immediate gradient divergence

beats.text: The villain is temporal correlation. Consecutive frames look nearly identical. Trapping the model in a deadly feedback loop of biased gradients.
beats.visual_focus: A chain of nearly identical sequential frames forming a suffocating closed loop, showing gradients repeating the same fatal mistake.

visual_blueprint.title: THE DEADLY CORRELATION TRAP
visual_blueprint.sub: Sequential data creates destructive positive feedback

motif_params.title: THE DEADLY CORRELATION TRAP
motif_params.sub: Sequential data creates destructive positive feedback

beats.text: The breakthrough is Experience Replay. Instead of learning live in real time. The agent stores past transitions inside a massive memory buffer.
beats.visual_focus: Transitions flying off the screen into a glowing circular memory vault, decoupling the agent's actions from immediate gradient calculation.

visual_blueprint.title: TAMING DEADLY FEED ARCHITECTURE
visual_blueprint.sub: Transitions flying off the screen into a glowing circular memory

beats.text: During each gradient step. The network samples random. Uniform batches across distant timelines. This shatters sequential correlation, keeping updates completely stationary.
beats.visual_focus: Visual code animation highlighting random mini-batch extraction from scattered points across the memory timeline into the loss function.
